Reference / random/source

random/source#

Stateful random sources with one compact capability.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let repeatable is Randomizing = PcgRandom(seed: 42);
let index is int = repeatable.integer(0, 10); // 0 through 9
let fraction is float = repeatable.float();   // 0.0 <= x < 1.0
let token is @byte = repeatable.bytes(16);

let secure is Randomizing = SecureRandom();
let nonce is @byte = secure.bytes(24);

Description#

Stateful random sources with one compact capability.

PcgRandom is PCG-XSH-RR 64/32 (pcg32), with multiplier 6364136223846793005 and fixed stream increment 1442695040888963407. Construction performs the standard zero-state advance, adds the signed seed modulo 2^64, then advances again. Each integer consumes pairs of 32-bit outputs until rejection sampling accepts one: a sample is one pair (high output first) per 64-bit word that stop - start - 1 needs, the first pair most significant, so a range up to 2^64 takes one pair per sample. float consumes two outputs and forms 53 random bits. bytes emits each 32-bit output little-endian; an incomplete final word discards its unused bytes. This sequence is part of the public reproducibility contract.

PcgRandom owns an opaque mutable stream. Copies of the object share that stream, just as copies of a reading capability share their underlying input. It is reproducible, not cryptographically secure. SecureRandom has no seed constructor and draws from the operating system's cryptographic generator: arc4random on Apple systems, getrandom elsewhere (served from the vDSO by glibc 2.41 on Linux 6.11 and later, one system call on older systems). Its integers take as many 64-bit samples as the range needs, so any non-empty range is accepted. Integer ranges are always non-empty and half-open [start, stop). Random byte requests are capped at 16 MiB per call.
